entries.proposition: Direction determines the phenotype. Two substitutions at one residue, A398E and A398V, have opposite effects on channel function and on seizures: the gain-of-function A398E patient developed generalised tonic-clonic seizures controlled on medication, while two unrelated A398V patients (partial loss of function) had developmental delay and microcephaly with no seizures.
entries.snippet: Seizures were also absent in the two unrelated patients with the A398V variant, correlating with the lack of hyperexcitability in the A398V NEURON model.

entries.proposition: The authors' reading of seizure risk from this and the earlier paper: substantial gain of Cav3.3 function leads to seizures, whereas both gain and loss of function can cause neurodevelopmental disease. This is a correlation across few patients; one gain-of-function patient (M1425V) had staring spells and no seizures.
entries.snippet: The hyperexcitability of TRN neurons expressing the gain-of-function variants correlates with the seizure phenotype in the patients with the M1425I and A398E variants.

entries.proposition: Generalisation by the authors: loss-of-function variants in voltage-gated calcium channels are linked to less severe developmental disorders with epilepsy a less frequent comorbidity than for gain-of-function variants. A T-type blocker would therefore be a mechanism-matched intervention for gain-of-function carriers and a mismatched or possibly harmful one for loss-of-function carriers: the genotype decides, and the paper shows no drug data of any kind.
entries.snippet: Generally, loss-of-function variants in voltage-gated calcium channels are linked to less severe cases of ID/DD, and epilepsy is less often a comorbidity compared to gain-of-function variants linked to ID/DD.

entries.proposition: Patient 4 (M1425V) had moderate intellectual disability, attention deficit and later psychosis with life-long staring spells but no seizures, a gain-of-function carrier without epilepsy, with behavioural and sleep abnormalities; the authors note the milder phenotype compared with M1425I correlates with milder gating effects.
entries.snippet: The 25-year-old male patient 4 with the p.(Met1425Val) variant had microcephaly, moderate ID, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, rigidity, and hyperacusis.
entries.anchor: Results, Four unrelated patients with a neurodevelopmental disorder

entries.proposition: Limits stated by the authors: the TRN neuron result is a computer simulation (heterozygous state mimicked as a 1:1 mix of channels) and the patients' mechanism of disease (calcium toxicity versus altered firing) is not resolved; further animal-model research is needed to say which pathways underlie the diverse phenotypes.
entries.snippet: Further research in animal models will have to elucidate which pathways, underlying the diverse neurodevelopmental phenotype, are affected by reduced versus increased CaV3.3 activity.
